passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Polycarp was instructed by apostles, conversed with many who had seen Christ, and was appointed bishop of Smyrna by apostles in Asia; Irenaeus saw him in his early youth. object_entity.notes: Bishop of Hierapolis in Asia Minor; wrote the Exposition of Dominical Oracles (5 books) c. 95-110, preserved by Eusebius; heard John the elder directly; key early witness for oral apostolic tradition and millenarianism.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Papias says he would not hesitate to expound along with the interpretations whatever he had ever learned from the elders and preserved in memory. He inquired about what the elders said — what Andrew or Peter said, what Philip or Thomas or James, what John or Matthew or any of the Lord's disciples.
passage.notes: Papias deliberately prefers oral tradition from those who knew the apostles; evidence for tradition-reception chain
